threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, product catalogue, and success criteria for the investment corner.

messages.text:
Kicking off the investment corner work for project_title: Launch of Hybrid Retail Investment Corner in Flagship Store.
From my side, I have a draft of the initial product and service list for T1 captured in A1. It focuses on simple, retail-friendly products: basic equity baskets, a conservative bond bundle, a starter ETF pack, and a low-risk savings-like product, plus a referral service for more complex mandates.
Before I lock T1, can everyone confirm:
1) Are these product types aligned with what you expect to sell in-store?
2) Any products you feel are too complex for walk-in customers given our constraints?
Once we agree, I will tag risk levels and target customer segments in A1 and send it to compliance for review.
Also, we should start thinking about the top metrics we want in A3 for the first month so we can design the tracker correctly.

Thanks for starting this.
From the store floor perspective, that mix sounds workable as long as the explanations in A1 stay very plain. I would avoid anything that requires long suitability checks at the counter.
Two questions:
- For the equity baskets and ETF pack, can we group them into simple themes (for example, income focus vs growth focus) so we can explain them quickly?
- For the referral service, will that be logged in A3 as a lead with some basic fields, or do you expect us to capture more detail?
Once we settle the list, I can align T2 and T6 so the scripts and process map match the catalogue.

From my side on the counter, I agree we should keep the list short at launch.
I would suggest:
- Keep the low-risk savings-like product very prominent.
- Limit the number of equity baskets and ETF packs so we can really learn the talking points.
Could we also add a simple educational leaflet service, like a basic guide to starting to invest, tied to T3? That might help with customers who are curious but not ready to buy.
For A3, I would like to track at least: number of walk-ins we talk to, number of products actually sold, and number of follow-up calls or emails scheduled.

Good starting point.
On the product side in A1, I would propose we explicitly exclude derivatives, leveraged products, and anything with complex tax treatment from the in-store catalogue for launch. Those can stay as referral-only topics.
For each product in T1, I will help define:
- Risk band (for example, low, medium, higher risk)
- Typical holding horizon
- Simple suitability notes (for example, not for short-term cash needs)
On metrics in A3, I suggest we shortlist candidates now and then narrow to three:
- Gross sales volume by product
- Number of qualified leads created
- Conversion rate from conversation to sale or referral
We can debate which three matter most for the first month.

From an accounting and compliance angle, I am comfortable with the direction as long as A1 clearly flags anything that is only a referral and not an in-store sale.
Two points I need to check while I work on T5 and T7:
- For the savings-like product, we must be precise about whether it is a deposit, a fund, or something else, because the accounting and tax treatment differ.
- For the metrics in A3, I would like at least one field that lets us reconcile to the general ledger easily, such as a simple product code.
I will draft a first version of the codes and share them when I have them, but I am fine if we first agree on the product list in A1 and then I adapt.

Quick note from logistics.
Once A1 is stable, I need to know roughly how many brochures or product sheets we will display so I can factor that into T4 and T8. If we have too many different leaflets, the stands might get messy and harder to keep stocked.
Also, if the referral service generates paperwork, please flag that so I can think about where that sits physically in the corner.

On the educational leaflet idea tied to T3, that fits well with the risk about complex explanations. We can treat that as a generic, non-product-specific piece that points to the safer products in A1 and to the referral service for anything more advanced.
On the catalogue itself, here is what I propose for launch in A1:
1) One low-risk savings-like product (capital preservation focus).
2) One conservative bond bundle.
3) One balanced equity basket.
4) One simple ETF pack.
5) A referral service for more complex mandates.
No derivatives, no leveraged products, and no tax-optimisation schemes in-store.
If there are no strong objections, I will enrich A1 with risk bands and target segments and send it to compliance today as part of T1.

The five-item list for A1 works for me.
From a sales conversation point of view, that is a manageable set to train on, and we can build clear talking points for each in T2.
For the metrics in A3, I would vote for:
- Number of customer conversations by product interest.
- Number of completed sales by product.
- Number of referrals created.
We can still capture sales volume in the background, but for the first month I think behaviour and conversion will tell us more than just amounts.

I am aligned with that list in A1 as well.
On the metrics, I like the idea of tracking conversations and referrals. Could we also have a simple field in A3 for customer type, like new to investing vs already investing? That will help us adjust the scripts later.
No further concerns from me on the catalogue.

On the success metrics, let me try to reconcile the different suggestions into three primary ones for A3:
1) Number of customer conversations by product interest.
2) Number of completed sales by product and total amount.
3) Number of referrals created and accepted.
We can add customer type as a field to slice these, but the three core metrics would be conversations, sales, and referrals.
If that sounds acceptable, we can treat these as the main success criteria for the first month and still allow finance to derive more detailed views from the same sheet.

Those three main metrics for A3 work for me, and they are easy to reconcile with the accounting view as long as we have product codes.
I will make sure T7 includes fields for product code, amount, customer type, and whether it is a sale or referral, but we can still highlight the three metrics you listed as the headline ones.
No objections from my side.

From logistics, those three metrics in A3 are fine. I just need to know if we will track anything about brochure stock there or if that stays in the daily checklist A4 later.
For now, I will assume A3 is focused on sales and leads, and A4 will cover physical checks.

Sounds like we have convergence.
To summarise and close on two points:
- Product catalogue in A1: we launch with the five items listed earlier (savings-like product, conservative bond bundle, balanced equity basket, simple ETF pack, and referral service), excluding derivatives, leveraged products, and complex tax schemes from in-store sales.
- Success metrics in A3: we track conversations by product interest, completed sales by product and amount, and referrals created and accepted, with customer type as an extra field.
Unless anyone objects today, I will treat this as approved for launch scope and move A1 to compliance review as part of T1, and I will brief the accountant on the fields for A3.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize customer scripts, education materials, and escalation rules.

messages.text:
I have put together a first draft of the customer sales and advisory script in A2 based on the approved catalogue in A1 and the metrics we want to track in A3.
The script for T2 follows four steps: greeting, discovery, explanation, and closing, with clear points where we either move to a simple product or create a referral.
I need feedback from traders and accounting on:
- Technical accuracy of the product explanations.
- Wording around risk and returns so we do not overpromise.
In parallel, we should align this with the simplified product sheets in T3 and the escalation rules in T11, which will be captured in A7.
Please review A2 and comment here before we freeze it.

I went through A2 and it feels natural to use at the counter.
A couple of observations from my side:
- In the discovery part, could we add one more question about how long the customer plans to keep the money invested? That will help us choose between the savings-like product and the other options.
- In the closing, we might want a standard line for when the customer is not ready to decide, pointing them to the educational leaflet from T3 and offering a follow-up.
On escalation, I would like very clear triggers in A7 so we do not hesitate when a question is too complex.

I have reviewed the product explanation sections in A2 against the catalogue in A1.
Overall, the descriptions are accurate, but I suggest a few adjustments:
- For the balanced equity basket, emphasise that values can go up and down and that it is meant for a medium-term horizon.
- For the ETF pack, avoid comparing it directly to a savings account; instead, explain diversification in simple terms.
I will also start drafting the one-page sheets for T3 so that the key phrases in A2 match the wording on the sheets. That way, what we say and what customers read are consistent.
On escalation rules in A7, I propose we treat any question about tax optimisation, leverage, or individual stock picking as an automatic escalation under T11.

Building on that, I would like A2 and A7 to share the same simple rule of thumb for escalation under T11:
- If the customer asks for a personalised portfolio recommendation beyond the four in-store products, escalate.
- If the customer mentions large sums above a threshold we will define, escalate.
- If the customer has complex tax or legal questions, escalate.
We can list these in A7 as bullet points and also include expected response times and channels.
I will help refine the technical parts of A2 and the product sheets in T3 so that the risk warnings are clear but not intimidating.

I have checked the draft A2 from an accounting and regulatory angle.
Two things we need to adjust:
- Remove any wording that sounds like guaranteed returns, especially for the bond bundle and ETF pack. We can talk about typical behaviour but not promises.
- Add a short reminder in the closing that all investments carry risk and that customers should only invest money they can set aside for the suggested horizon.
Once those changes are in, I am comfortable that A2 does not conflict with what we will document in A5.
For A7, I would like the escalation rules to include a note that any complaint or sign of dissatisfaction is logged and escalated as well, even if the question itself is simple.

Thanks for the detailed feedback.
I will update A2 to:
- Add the investment horizon question in discovery.
- Remove any language that sounds like a promise and replace it with neutral descriptions.
- Add a standard closing line about risk and only investing money that can be set aside.
For A7 and T11, I will draft the escalation triggers based on what you and the traders suggested: complex tax or legal questions, large sums, personalised portfolios beyond the four products, and any complaint or discomfort.
I will share an updated A2 and a first draft of A7 shortly.

I have also progressed T3 in parallel.
For each product in A1, the one-page sheet will include:
- Plain-language description.
- Simple risk band and horizon.
- Key warnings and disclaimers aligned with A2.
- A short section that says when this product may not be suitable.
Once your updated A2 is ready, I will cross-check the wording so that the script and the sheets reinforce each other.
On A7, I support the escalation triggers you listed. We should also specify the contact channel (for example, dedicated phone line and email) and typical response times so store staff know what to tell customers.

When you update A2, could you also add a short branch for customers who only want information and do not want to share personal details yet? Something like offering the leaflet from T3 and inviting them to come back.
For A7, it would help if we had a simple checklist we can glance at during a conversation to decide whether to escalate under T11. Maybe that can be a small section at the end of A2 as well.

I have reviewed the near-final A2 and the draft A7 you shared.
From my side, the technical content is sound, the risk wording is balanced, and the escalation triggers under T11 are clear and practical.
I suggest we lock A2 now so that training and T6 can move forward. Any minor tweaks later can be handled as version updates, but the core flow looks ready for launch.

I agree with locking A2 now.
I have rechecked the latest version and it aligns with our constraints and with what I am drafting in A5. The risk and return language is now neutral and does not create accounting or regulatory issues.
On A7, I am comfortable with the escalation criteria and the note about logging complaints. We just need to make sure the contact details and response times are kept up to date, but that can be part of our regular maintenance.

Thanks everyone.
To summarise where we landed:
- A2 is approved as the launch script for T2, covering greeting, discovery (including horizon and risk questions), explanation, and closing, with clear branches for information-only visits and for referrals.
- A7 captures the escalation rules for T11: complex tax or legal questions, large sums above the agreed threshold, personalised portfolios beyond the four products, and any complaint or discomfort, with defined channels and response times.
Unless there are last-minute objections today, I will treat both A2 and A7 as signed off for launch and move on to aligning T6 and the training content.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on layout, logistics plan, and move schedule for the investment corner.

messages.text:
I have drafted a first version of the layout and move plan in A6 for T4 and T8.
The idea is to place the investment corner near the customer service desk, using existing floor space so we do not exceed the allocation. The sketch in A6 shows:
- A main counter with two seats for customers.
- A brochure stand for the product sheets from T3.
- A small storage cabinet for extra materials.
For T8, I propose doing the physical move after store closing over two evenings to reduce disruption.
Please review A6 and let me know if the position, furniture, or move timing creates any issues.

Thanks for sharing A6.
From a customer flow perspective, being near the customer service desk makes sense, but we need to be sure there is enough privacy for financial conversations.
Looking at your sketch, could we:
- Add a small divider or screen behind the customer chairs to reduce noise from the main aisle?
- Make sure the brochure stand is visible from the aisle so people can pick up leaflets without committing to a full conversation?
On T8, two evenings after closing sounds fine to me as long as we can still access the area the next morning without safety issues.

I agree with the location in A6, but I share the concern about privacy.
Also, could we have a small space on the counter for a laptop or tablet so we can access A3 and the scripts in A2 during conversations? That might affect the furniture plan in T4.
For T8, it would help if we had a simple checklist of what needs to be moved and tested each evening so we do not forget things like power outlets or network connections.

From the trading side, the main concern is that the corner is safe and practical for handling customer data and any paperwork.
In A6, can we ensure:
- There is a lockable drawer or cabinet for any printed forms.
- The screen is positioned so that passers-by cannot easily see sensitive information.
On T8, I support doing the move after hours. We should also plan a short dry run once everything is in place so we can test the flow with A4 and A3 before launch.

Looking at A6, I just want to flag a couple of points from an accounting and control perspective:
- We should avoid placing any cash handling in the investment corner itself; all payments should go through the existing tills, and A5 will reflect that.
- If we store any signed documents, the lockable cabinet you mentioned should be part of the layout and included in the daily checks in A4.
On T8, please make sure we have a quick handover note after the move so I know where any physical documents will be kept.

Thanks for the comments.
I can update A6 to:
- Add a low divider behind the customer chairs to improve privacy without blocking visibility.
- Move the brochure stand slightly closer to the aisle so customers can grab leaflets easily.
I will also adjust T4 to include a lockable cabinet and enough counter space for a laptop or tablet, as suggested.
For T8, I will draft a simple move checklist that covers furniture, power, network, and safety checks each evening.

Those adjustments in A6 sound good to me.
One more detail: can we make sure there is a clear line of sight from the main aisle to at least one of the risk warning posters from T3? That will reinforce the messages from A2 even before customers sit down.
Otherwise, I am comfortable with the updated layout and the idea of a move checklist under T8.

Good point.
I will add a wall-mounted frame for a key risk warning poster in A6, positioned so it is visible from the aisle but still close to the corner.
I will also note in T4 that the poster is part of the standard setup and in T8 that we need to install it during the move.
Once I have the updated sketch, I will upload it to A6.

With the divider, lockable storage, and poster placement added to A6, I am comfortable with the layout.
For T8, could you propose specific dates and times for the two evening moves, ideally leaving at least one full day before launch for us to test the corner using A4 and A3?
Once we have those dates, we can share them with store operations for final confirmation.

For T8, I propose the following schedule:
- Evening 1: move furniture, install divider, and set up the brochure stand and poster frame.
- Evening 2: connect power and network, place materials, and run basic safety checks.
Both evenings would start one hour after store closing and last about two hours.
This leaves the full next day for you to test the corner with A4 and A3.
If store operations agree with these time windows, I can treat this as the final move plan in A6.

The proposed T8 schedule works for me.
Please just make sure that any lockable storage for documents is installed and tested on Evening 2 so we can include it in the daily checks in A4 and in the process description in A5.
No further comments on A6 from my side.

Given the updates and the proposed schedule, I suggest we close on two points:
- Approve the updated layout and logistics plan in A6, including the divider, brochure stand position, lockable cabinet, and risk poster placement, as the final plan for T4.
- Confirm the two-evening after-hours move schedule in T8 as you described, subject only to store operations confirming the exact dates.
This will let us move on to testing the corner with A4 and preparing for training.

threads.thread_goal: Lock down accounting, tracking, and reporting processes before launch.

messages.text:
I have prepared a draft of the accounting and reporting process in A5, plus initial structures for A3 and A8, based on T5, T7, and T12.
Key points in A5:
- Dedicated product codes for each of the five catalogue items in A1.
- All cash movements go through existing tills; the corner records sales and leads but does not handle cash.
- A simple reconciliation process between A3 and the general ledger at month-end.
For A3, I have included fields for date, product code, amount, customer type, conversation outcome (sale, referral, information only), and staff member.
For A8, the week 1 review template, I have sections for sales and leads summary, key issues, and improvement ideas.
Please review and let me know if anything is missing or impractical before we finalise.

Thanks for pulling this together.
Looking at A3, the fields you listed cover the three main metrics we agreed in TH1. I would just add a simple flag for whether a referral was accepted by the trading desk, so we can distinguish created vs converted referrals.
In A5, the reconciliation process looks reasonable. One suggestion: can we schedule a quick daily spot check between A3 and the tills for the first week, not just month-end, to catch any issues early?
For A8, I would like a small section where traders and sellers can add qualitative feedback on customer understanding of the products.

I agree with the overall structure in A5.
On the chart of accounts in T5, the dedicated product codes per item in A1 will help us analyse performance by product. We should also consider a simple cost centre for the investment corner so we can track any direct costs separately.
For A3, I support adding the referral acceptance flag and maybe a field for follow-up date when relevant.
On A8, I suggest we include a short section for risk or compliance incidents, even if the expectation is that this stays empty. That will keep us honest in the week 1 review.

From the store side, A3 looks usable as long as we keep the number of mandatory fields manageable during busy times.
Could we:
- Make product code, amount (for sales), and outcome mandatory.
- Treat customer type and follow-up date as recommended but not blocking fields.
For A8, I like the idea of a section for customer understanding and another for what worked well in the scripts from A2. That will help us refine T2 and T6 after week 1.

I agree with keeping A3 simple to fill in.
One practical question: will A3 be a shared sheet we access from the counter, or will we log entries at the end of the day? For accuracy, I would prefer logging right after each conversation if possible.
On A8, it would be helpful to have a small space to note common customer questions that were not covered well by A2 or the product sheets from T3, so we can improve them.

Thanks for the suggestions.
I will update A3 to include:
- A referral acceptance flag.
- An optional follow-up date field.
- Clear indication of which fields are mandatory vs recommended, as you proposed.
In A5, I will add a short daily spot check for the first week, comparing A3 entries with till reports for the investment products.
For A8, I will add sections for qualitative feedback on customer understanding, script effectiveness, and any risk or compliance incidents.

That works for me.
One more detail for A5: when we define the reconciliation process under T5, can we specify who is responsible each day and at month-end? For example, store supervisor for daily checks and finance for month-end.
This will avoid confusion once we go live.

Good point.
I will update A5 so that T5 clearly assigns:
- Daily spot checks in week 1 to the store supervisor, using A3 and till reports.
- Month-end reconciliation to the finance team, using A3 and the general ledger.
I will also note that any discrepancies found should be logged and reviewed in the week 1 A8 template.

With these updates, I think A5 now covers the key accounting and compliance aspects for the corner.
The dedicated product codes, clear cash handling rules, and defined responsibilities for reconciliation give us a solid base.
Unless anyone sees a gap, I suggest we approve A5 so we can focus on training and launch readiness.

I am comfortable with A5 as it stands.
A3 looks manageable for the team to fill in, and A8 will give us a structured way to capture what we learn in week 1.
No further changes requested from my side.

Same here.
As long as we have quick access to A3 at the counter and clear guidance on when to fill it in, the process in A5 feels workable.
I like that A8 includes space for common questions and script improvements; that will help us refine A2 and T2 after launch.

Thanks all.
To summarise:
- A5 is approved as the accounting and compliance process for the investment corner under T5, including dedicated product codes, cash handling rules, and reconciliation responsibilities.
- A3 is agreed as the daily tracker structure under T7, with fields for the three main metrics plus referral acceptance and follow-up date.
- A8 is agreed as the week 1 review template under T12, with sections for quantitative results, customer understanding, script effectiveness, and any incidents.
I will treat A5, A3, and A8 as final for launch unless we uncover issues during testing.

threads.thread_goal: Coordinate training, go-live checklist, and launch day responsibilities.

messages.text:
With A1, A2, A5, and A6 now in good shape, we should lock in training and the daily operations checklist.
For T9, I propose a joint training session next week, 2 hours, in the training room near the store. Agenda:
- Overview of the product catalogue in A1.
- Walk-through of the script in A2.
- Demo of the layout from A6 and the daily tracker A3.
- Q&A and escalation rules from A7.
Does that timing work for everyone, and are there any topics you want to add?
In parallel, we need to finalise the daily checklist in A4 under T10 so that opening, mid-day, and closing routines are clear for launch.

The proposed training format for T9 works for me.
I would add a short role-play segment where we practice the script in A2 with typical customer profiles, including at least one escalation scenario using A7.
On A4 and T10, I have a draft checklist that covers:
- Opening: materials stocked, systems on, risk posters visible.
- Mid-day: quick stock check, A3 entries up to date.
- Closing: secure documents in the lockable cabinet, log any incidents, and back up A3.
I will share the draft A4 shortly for comments.

I can attend the training at the proposed time.
For T9, it would help if we also cover how to handle customers who only want information and do not want to share details yet, using the branches in A2 and the leaflets from T3.
On A4, I like the structure you described. Maybe we can add a quick check that the screen is positioned correctly so others cannot see customer data, and that the lockable cabinet is closed at mid-day and closing.

I can join the training for at least part of the session.
For T9, I would like a short slot to explain the physical layout from A6, how to keep the area tidy, and what to do if something is damaged or out of place.
On A4 and T10, please include a simple check that the divider, brochure stand, and risk poster are in the right position and that there are no boxes or obstacles in the customer path.

I can attend the training as well.
For T9, I would like to cover briefly:
- How A3 entries link to accounting.
- What to do if there is a discrepancy or a complaint, tying back to A5 and A7.
On A4, please add a reminder to check that no documents are left on the counter at closing and that any incident is noted for the week 1 review in A8.

Great, thanks for the inputs.
For T9, I will structure the session as follows:
1) Product overview (A1).
2) Script walk-through and role-plays (A2).
3) Layout and logistics (A6) with your segment.
4) Tracking and accounting (A3, A5).
5) Escalation rules and complaints (A7).
6) Q&A.
I will propose a specific date and time: next Wednesday, 10:00–12:00. If anyone has a conflict, please flag it today so we can adjust.

Next Wednesday 10:00–12:00 works for me.
I will finalise the draft A4 for T10 today with the points we discussed and share it so we can review it quickly before the training. It would be good if we can walk through A4 during the session as well so everyone understands their responsibilities.

The proposed training time works for me too.
On A4, once your draft is ready, I can check that the opening and closing steps match what we actually do on the floor and suggest any small tweaks.
I also suggest we include a quick reminder in A4 to test access to A2 and A3 at opening, so we do not discover access issues in the middle of the day.

Next Wednesday works for me as well.
For A4 and T10, please add a simple check that the area is free of trip hazards and that any boxes from deliveries are moved away from the customer path before opening.
I will also prepare a short visual of the correct layout from A6 to show during the training.

The training slot works for me.
On A4, I would just add that at closing we should confirm that A3 entries for the day are complete and that any discrepancies or complaints are noted for follow-up in A5 and A8.
Otherwise, the checklist structure you described sounds good.

I have now updated A4 for T10 with all the suggestions:
- Opening: check layout from A6, systems access to A2 and A3, materials stocked, risk posters visible, area free of obstacles.
- Mid-day: quick stock and cleanliness check, confirm A3 entries are up to date, cabinet locked when not in use.
- Closing: secure documents, confirm no papers left on the counter, final A3 check, note any incidents for A8.
Please take a quick look and confirm there is nothing missing before we call it final.

I have reviewed A4 and it matches what we need on the floor.
The only small addition I would suggest is a reminder at opening to check that the escalation contact details from A7 are visible or easily accessible, so we do not waste time looking for them during a conversation.
Otherwise, I am happy to use this checklist from day one.

Good catch.
I have added to A4 under opening: confirm escalation contacts from A7 are visible or bookmarked.
With that, I think A4 is ready to be our launch checklist for T10.

It sounds like we have alignment.
To close this out:
- Training session for T9 is confirmed for next Wednesday, 10:00–12:00, with the agenda we outlined (A1, A2, A6, A3, A5, A7, and A4 walk-through).
- A4 is approved as the daily operations checklist for T10, covering opening, mid-day, and closing checks, including layout, materials, systems, security, and incident logging.
I will send a short invite summarising the agenda and link to A4 so store staff can review it before the session.
